s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute onset of painful swelling and muscle weakness with systemic inflammation and multi-organ involvement
salient_findings: Painful swelling of the calves
Elevated muscle enzymes (CK, LDH)
Diffuse subcutaneous edema on CT scan
Muscle biopsy showing interstitial and perivascular infiltrates
Cardiac involvement with myocarditis and arrhythmias
Neurologic findings with myelitis and encephalitis
key_facts: 57-year-old man with history of mantle cell lymphoma in complete remission
Presented with painful swelling of the calves in August 2018
No evidence of deep venous thrombosis or soft-tissue infection
Brief gastroenteritis episode prior to presentation
Diuretics provided transient relief
Systemic steroids and discontinuation of ibrutinib had no effect
Elevated LDH and CK on laboratory tests
Negative autoimmune serology
CT scan showed diffuse subcutaneous edema
MRI of the thighs showed diffuse intramuscular and extramuscular edema
Muscle biopsy demonstrated interstitial and perivascular T-cell and macrophage infiltrates
Developed acute kidney injury secondary to rhabdomyolysis
Cardiac MRI confirmed myocarditis
Spinal MRI demonstrated a hyperintense lesion concerning for myelitis
CSF analysis showed elevated leukocyte count, lactate, and protein

shortlist.label: Polymyositis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated CK, muscle biopsy with interstitial and perivascular T-cell and macrophage infiltrates

shortlist.label: Dermatomyositis
shortlist.why_kept: Painful swelling and muscle weakness, although skin manifestations are not explicitly mentioned

shortlist.label: Necrotizing autoimmune myopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated CK, muscle biopsy with necrosis and regeneration, and rhabdomyolysis

shortlist.label: Ibrutinib-induced myopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Patient was on ibrutinib, which is a known cause of myopathy

shortlist.label: Myocarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Cardiac MRI confirmed myocarditis, suggesting a systemic inflammatory process

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with painful swelling of the calves, elevated LDH and CK, and muscle biopsy demonstrating interstitial and perivascular T-cell and macrophage infiltrates with necrosis and regeneration are consistent with necrotizing autoimmune myopathy. The lack of response to systemic steroids and the presence of rhabdomyolysis also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Polymyositis
rejected.why: While the patient's muscle biopsy shows interstitial and perivascular infiltrates, the presence of necrosis and regeneration is more characteristic of necrotizing autoimmune myopathy.

rejected.label: Dermatomyositis
rejected.why: There is no mention of skin manifestations, which are a hallmark of dermatomyositis.

rejected.label: Ibrutinib-induced myopathy
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms persisted after discontinuation of ibrutinib, suggesting that the myopathy is not solely due to the medication.

rejected.label: Myocarditis
rejected.why: While the patient did develop myocarditis, the primary presentation and muscle biopsy findings suggest a more widespread myopathic process, rather than isolated myocarditis.
